title: B2 · L6 — Advanced passive
topic: Impersonal passive structures with reporting verbs
description: Estructuras pasivas impersonales: 'It is said that...', 'He is thought to...'. Muy usadas en noticias, informes y contextos formales.

questions.prompt: Situación: lees un titular de la sección de negocios del Financial Times.
questions.question: Complete: 'It ___ that the CEO will resign next month.'
questions.explanation: 'It is thought/said/believed that...' es la fórmula pasiva impersonal por excelencia en registro periodístico. Permite reportar rumores u opiniones colectivas SIN atribuir la fuente — ideal cuando la información no está confirmada. Error típico: usar la voz activa ('People think that...') que suena más informal y menos profesional.
examples: It is thought that talks will resume next week. → titular económico
It is widely believed that the artefact is over 2,000 years old. → registro académico

questions.prompt: Transformas una frase para una biografía formal.
questions.question: Transform: 'People say he is very rich.'
options: He is said to be very rich.
He said to be very rich.
He is saying to be rich.
questions.explanation: La estructura personal es 'Subject + is said/thought/believed + TO + infinitivo'. Es alternativa más elegante a 'It is said that he is rich' — desplaza el sujeto al principio y suena menos pesada. Muy común en biografías, perfiles de prensa y textos académicos. NUNCA omitir el 'to be' — 'He is said very rich' es un error grave.
examples: She is believed to be one of the youngest CEOs in Silicon Valley.
They are thought to be responsible for the security breach. → nota corporativa

questions.statement: 'He is said to have written the book' se refiere a una acción pasada.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. La estructura 'to have + participio' tras el verbo reportado marca anterioridad: la acción ocurrió ANTES de que se diga la frase. Compara: 'He is said to write' (escribe ahora) vs 'He is said to have written' (escribió en el pasado). Es un mecanismo clave para hablar de rumores sobre acciones ya consumadas.
examples: She is thought to have left the country under a false name. → titular de investigación
The suspect is believed to have escaped through the tunnel last night.

questions.text: The painting is believed to have been stolen during the war.
questions.explanation: Doble pasiva: 'is believed to have been stolen' combina pasiva del verbo reportado + pasiva del acontecimiento. Connected speech: 'to have' colapsa a 'təv' /təv/, y 'have been' se fusiona con schwa → 'əv-bɪn'. Es la cadencia clásica de reportaje de arte, museos o crimen histórico.
examples: The document is believed to have been destroyed in the 1930s. → historia del archivo
The treasure is thought to have been hidden somewhere along the coast.

questions.prompt: Analizas cuáles verbos encajan en la estructura pasiva impersonal.
questions.question: Which reporting verb is NOT typically used in this passive structure?
questions.explanation: 'Want' expresa deseo personal, no una creencia u opinión colectiva reportable, así que no encaja en la pasiva impersonal. Los verbos válidos son de PERCEPCIÓN/JUICIO COLECTIVO: say, believe, think, know, report, allege, claim, consider, understand, estimate, rumour, expect. Truco: si el verbo se puede sustituir por 'creer/pensar/decir', probablemente funciona.
examples: It is reported that talks between the two nations have collapsed. → noticia diplomática
The suspect is alleged to have fled the country hours before the arrest.

questions.statement: 'It is said that he is guilty' y 'He is said to be guilty' significan lo mismo.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Son estructuralmente equivalentes y transmiten la misma información. La diferencia es estilística: la primera ('It is said that...') es más común en registro hablado y explicaciones; la segunda ('He is said to be...') es más frecuente en escritura periodística y suena más elegante y compacta.
examples: It is said that she is a great teacher. = She is said to be a great teacher.
It is thought that they have arrived. = They are thought to have arrived. → mismo significado, distinto ritmo

questions.prompt: Empareja cada verbo reportado con su continuación natural:

pairs.right: to be the richest woman in the country.

questions.explanation: Cada verbo tiene su registro típico: 'said' es neutro; 'believed/thought' son de opinión general; 'alleged' es JURÍDICO (implica acusación no probada); 'understood' es formal e informativo (típico en briefings). Elegir el verbo correcto cambia el matiz de certeza/formalidad.
examples: The report is said to be strictly confidential. → registro corporativo
The prime minister is understood to have resigned late last night. → boletín de última hora

questions.prompt: Reescribes un cotilleo para el perfil de una revista.
questions.question: Rewrite: 'They say she has been ill for months.'
options: She is said to have been ill for months.
She is said to be ill for months.
She is said she has been ill for months.
It is said she is ill for months.
questions.explanation: El present perfect ('has been') se transforma en 'to have been' tras 'is said'. La duración con 'for months' se mantiene intacta. Regla útil: si el verbo original está en presente perfect o pasado simple, la pasiva usa 'to have + PP'; si está en presente simple, usa 'to be'.
examples: He is said to have been living abroad since 2010. → perfil biográfico
They are believed to have been married in secret for decades.

questions.target: The company is believed to have suffered significant losses in the last quarter.
questions.explanation: Registro periodístico económico, típico de radio (BBC, NPR) o podcast financiero. Prosodia: ritmo pausado y neutral, con énfasis en 'significant losses'. Reducción típica: 'to have' → /təv/. Nativos añaden hedging al reportar noticias no confirmadas: 'according to industry sources...', 'reportedly...'.
examples: The bank is thought to have made record profits despite the market turmoil.
The startup is said to have raised over 200 million dollars in Series C funding.

questions.prompt: Un editor te explica por qué usar la pasiva impersonal en un artículo.
questions.question: Which structure is used when we don't know or don't want to reveal the agent?
options: Impersonal passive with 'it is said that'.
questions.explanation: La pasiva impersonal es la herramienta editorial clave para reportar información sin comprometer a una fuente específica: rumores, filtraciones, opiniones generalizadas. Aporta objetividad aparente y protege al periodista. Es lo contrario a la voz activa con 'people say', que suena vago y coloquial.
examples: It is claimed that he acted alone, though investigators remain sceptical. → nota policial
It is thought that global temperatures will rise by 2°C by 2050. → informe científico

questions.statement: En escritura formal, la pasiva impersonal ayuda a sonar más objetivo.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Al eliminar el agente subjetivo ('yo creo', 'la gente dice'), la información se presenta como consenso o dato neutro. Es un rasgo estilístico central del inglés académico y periodístico. Ojo: en escritura moderna se recomienda no abusar — demasiada pasiva impersonal suena evasiva o pretenciosa.
examples: It is generally accepted that climate change is largely human-driven. → paper científico
The theory is widely believed to explain the origins of the phenomenon.

questions.text: It is widely believed that regular exercise significantly improves mental health.
questions.explanation: Frase de artículo divulgativo tipo Guardian/Atlantic. Prosodia formal, ritmo pausado. Nota el adverbio intensificador 'widely' delante de 'believed' — es un patrón fijo (widely believed, widely accepted, widely used) que añade fuerza al consenso reportado. 'Significantly' es otra colocación clásica del inglés académico.
examples: It is generally accepted that quality sleep is essential to cognitive performance.
It is commonly thought that meditation reduces stress, though the evidence is mixed.

questions.prompt: Un guía de museo te muestra un manuscrito.
questions.question: Complete: 'The manuscript ___ to date back to the 12th century.'
questions.explanation: 'Is estimated to' es la fórmula estándar en contextos científicos, académicos y arqueológicos para reportar cálculos o dataciones sin atribuirlos a una fuente concreta. Combina bien con 'to date back to', 'to reach', 'to weigh', 'to cost' — colocaciones típicas de divulgación técnica.
examples: The building is estimated to be around 500 years old, based on carbon dating.
The world population is estimated to reach 10 billion by 2050. → informe demográfico

questions.target: The suspect is alleged to have entered the building through a back window shortly after midnight.
questions.explanation: Registro periodístico-legal. 'Alleged' es la palabra clave: implica acusación NO probada y protege al medio de posibles demandas por difamación. Prosodia neutra, ritmo pausado, sin cargas emocionales. Nativos periodistas casi siempre añaden 'reportedly' o 'according to police sources' para reforzar la distancia editorial.
examples: The politician is alleged to have accepted bribes from three separate contractors. → titular de investigación
The company is alleged to have violated safety regulations on multiple occasions.

questions.question: Which sentence is INCORRECT?
options: It is known that she works there.
She is known to work there.
She is known to working there.
She is known to have worked there.
questions.explanation: Tras 'is known/said/believed/thought' se usa infinitivo con 'to' + verbo base ('to work') o infinitivo perfecto ('to have + PP'). NUNCA '-ing'. Este es uno de los errores más frecuentes en exámenes B2 First porque los hispanohablantes confunden esta estructura con 'used to' o con gerundios tras preposición.
examples: Correct: She is known to be an expert in medieval literature. → forma simple
Correct: She is known to have worked at Google for over a decade. → forma perfecta
